newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 10-year benchmark bond seen expensive.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 10-year benchmark bond seen expensive.

text.p: The Dutch 10-year benchmark bond, the 5.75 percent February 2007, is trading rich despite the reopening of tap sales last week, two banks said on Monday.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said in its Bond Weekly publication that the Dutch bond market had outperformed Germany since mid-May despite the reopening of tap sales.
"In relative value terms, the tap issue did not cheapen up and it is still trading four basis points rich to the curve, which shows there was final investor demand," it said.
The tap issue raised 5.0 billion guilders in four days at an average price of 99.49 and an average yield of 5.82 percent.
This increased to 12.5 billion guilders the amount on issue in the 10-year bellwether state loan.
Rabobank International said its Financial Weekly publication that the tap issue was placed smoothly, with major parts of the issue going to a few big buyers.
It said the spread discount to comparative 10-year German Bunds widened due to increased political uncertainty in Germany and France.
But Rabobank said spread could not be used as a measure of whether the Dutch bond was expensive, adding it preferred to look at the difference between fair value and market price.
"Our calculations show that this spread increased somewhat last week," it said.
But, given the increased liquidity of the bond, the higher spread was justified.
A Rabobank spokesman said the February 2007 bond was now trading at a 27 cent, or three basis point, premium to fair value.
